full_text_en:
Yang Peikang v. Wuxi Huoli Health Products Co., Ltd.

— dispute over infringement of invention patent

【Ruling Summary】

A litigation settlement agreement is a consensus reached by the parties to a case to terminate a dispute or prevent a recurrence of the dispute through mutual concessions. The content of the settlement agreement is not limited to the claims made by the parties in the litigation.

When a party has a relatively high level of education and has been represented by an attorney who participated in the litigation, mediation, and settlement activities, and the party signed and agreed to the settlement agreement and accepted the payment made by the other party in accordance with the settlement agreement, and subsequently applies for retrial on the ground that the mediation was contrary to its true intention, such application for retrial does not meet the circumstances specified in Article 182 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and shall be dismissed.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2008) Min Shen Zi No. 1185

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Yang Peikang, male, Han ethnicity, born on April 24, 1943, residing at Room 66, East Street, Qianhuang Town, Wujin District, Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Boyuan, male, Han ethnicity, born on January 24, 1956, residing at Room 607, Building C4, Ministry of Construction Compound, Beijing.

Agent ad litem: Xu Rui, female, Han ethnicity, born on January 18, 1978, residing at Dongyidui, Qianhuang Town, Wujin District, Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

Respondent to the Retrial Application (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Wuxi Huoli Health Products Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 127 Huiqian Road, Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Mei Xianbao, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Cheng Xiaoyu, lawyer, Jiangsu Zhengtaihe Law Firm.

Applicant for retrial, Yang Peikang, filed an application for retrial with this Court, dissatisfied with the Civil Mediation Document (2008) Su Min San Zhong Zi No. 0038 of the Jiangsu High People's Court, in connection with the dispute over infringement of invention patent with the Respondent to the Retrial Application, Wuxi Huoli Health Products Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huoli Company). This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to review this case, and the review has now been completed.

Yang Peikang applied for retrial on the following grounds: 1. The settlement agreement was not reached voluntarily by the parties themselves but was arranged by the presiding judge of the second instance court. 2. In this litigation, Yang Peikang only requested the court to order Huoli Company to cease the infringement, and the claim for damages was to be filed in a separate lawsuit. However, the mediation document issued by the second instance court resolved the damages together with the infringement claim, misunderstanding Yang Peikang's true intention and disrupting his litigation plan. 3. The amount of damages in the second instance mediation document was not determined in accordance with Article 60 of the Patent Law.

Huoli Company argued in its defense: 1. The second instance civil mediation document was made in accordance with the "Settlement Agreement" signed by both parties. This settlement agreement was voluntarily signed by both parties after considerable deliberation and consideration, with Yang Peikang's personal signature confirming it. It represented the true intention of both parties, and its content did not violate legal provisions. 2. Yang Peikang has full capacity for civil conduct, a relatively high level of education, and knowledge of the law. He should have been fully aware of the legal consequences of signing the settlement agreement. Furthermore, his attorney participated in the entire process of the trial and mediation, so there could be no "misunderstanding" as claimed by Yang Peikang.

Upon review, this Court finds the following facts: In November 2005, Yang Peikang filed a lawsuit with the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, alleging that Huoli Company had infringed his patent rights. He requested the court to confirm the infringement by Huoli Company and order Huoli Company to cease production and sale of the allegedly infringing products. The court of first instance found that the allegedly infringing products produced and sold by Huoli Company fell within the scope of protection of the patent right, constituted infringement of Yang Peikang's patent right, and that Huoli Company should bear corresponding civil liability in accordance with the law. Accordingly, the court ruled that Huoli Company must immediately cease production and sale of the allegedly infringing products after the judgment took effect. Huoli Company, dissatisfied with this judgment, appealed to the Jiangsu High People's Court. During the second instance trial, with the mediation of the court, the parties reached a settlement agreement. The second instance court issued a civil mediation document based on this settlement agreement.

Further investigation reveals that on May 19, 2008, Yang Peikang and Huoli Company signed a "Settlement Agreement," which was signed by Yang Peikang personally and the specially authorized agent of Huoli Company. Yang Peikang's attorney participated in the second instance trial and the settlement and mediation activities. Yang Peikang has received RMB 55,000 paid by Huoli Company in accordance with the settlement agreement.

This Court holds that a litigation settlement agreement is a consensus reached by the parties to a case through mutual concessions to terminate their dispute or prevent its recurrence. The content of the settlement agreement is not limited to the claims made by the parties in the litigation. In this case, Yang Peikang had a relatively high level of education, and his attorney participated together with him in the trial and the settlement and mediation activities. Yang Peikang personally signed the settlement agreement and accepted the payment made by Huoli Company in accordance with the agreement. Therefore, the circumstances claimed by Yang Peikang that "the mediation was contrary to his true intention" or that the principle of voluntary mediation was violated do not exist in this case. Moreover, the content of the settlement agreement does not violate the law. The second instance court properly made the mediation document in accordance with the settlement agreement signed by both parties. Yang Peikang's application for retrial does not meet the circumstances specified in Article 182 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to the provisions of Article 181, paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

The application for retrial by Yang Peikang is dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Wang Yongchang

Acting Judge: Xi Zhonglin

Acting Judge: Li Jian

December 22, 2008

Clerk: Wang Xin
